fields.value: Move errors, storage, records and checkpoints out of etude.tracking to the top level

## Problem

`etude.tracking` is the shared run layer for training and evaluation, but it also holds four general Etude building blocks. Evaluation imports them from `tracking`, which makes `tracking` look like more than it is.

## Outcome

Move each one to a top-level module and import it from there:

| Now in `etude.tracking` | Moves to |
| -- | -- |
| `errors.EtudeError` | `etude/errors.py` |
| `storage` (`Storage`, `DirectoryStorage`, `S3Storage`, `SAFE_NAME`, `default_root`, `run_prefix`) | `etude/storage.py`, beside `cache.py` and `carriage.py` |
| base record types (`Record`, `Digest`, `Name`, `RunFile`) | `etude/records.py` |
| `checkpoints` (`CheckpointRecord`, `CheckpointRef`, `CheckpointId`, `checkpoint_id`) | `etude/checkpoints.py` |

What stays in `etude.tracking` is the run itself: `declare`, delivery (`ship`, `destinations`, `RunFiles`, `StorageDestination`), outcome records (`RunState`, `RunCounters`), and listing (`run_folders`, `under`, `as_storage`). `tests/run/test_layout.py` keeps its rule that tracking imports no kind of run. Add the matching rule for the new modules: they import none of tracking, train, eval or launch. Revisit the name `tracking` only if it still reads wrong after the split.

Jack Heart, 2026-11-13, on the table above: "agreed".

## Constraints

* Starts after EXP-56 (PR loopflowstudio/etude#103) lands. That PR is mid-rename and created several of these modules; moving them now would conflict.
* Renamed public Python names keep a warning alias until release 0.5, as EXP-56 does.
* No other behaviour changes. Check the module import counts in the start-up tests.
